title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Tanzania: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Tanzania: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Tanzania: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: Managing medical documentation, legal capacity planning, social security incapacity entitlements, and civil records during a serious or terminal illness in the United Republic of Tanzania involves distinct civil and institutional rules between Mainland Tanzania and Zanzibar alongside shared pension, tax, and consular legalization frameworks.

steps.title: Clinical Care, Medical Summaries, and Capacity Safeguards
steps.html:
• Request comprehensive specialist clinical summaries, diagnostic documentation, treatment histories, and certified medical board opinions through hospital curative and palliative care departments regulated under the Ministry of Health, as formal clinical evidence is required for disability benefit applications and court capacity reviews [1][2][7].
  • Review statutory safeguards for persons experiencing impaired decision-making capacity under the Mental Health Act (Cap. 98), which governs clinical evaluation, inpatient consent protections, and court guardianship orders over estate and financial affairs [10].

steps.title: Powers of Attorney, Wills, and RITA Safe Custody
steps.html:
• Execute a formal written Power of Attorney before cognitive capacity declines so a trusted attorney-in-fact can manage banking mandates, tax filings, or property transactions in Tanzania [9].
  • Prepare a written will aligned with the Probate and Administration of Estates Act (Cap. 352) and Registration, Insolvency and Trusteeship Agency (RITA) trusteeship guidelines, which note that written wills are attested by two witnesses (one clan relative and one independent witness) while oral wills require four witnesses (two clan members and two independent witnesses) [3][4][9].
  • Deposit the original will with RITA for official safe custody so appointed executors or family administrators can retrieve it promptly when needed [3][4].

steps.title: Invalidity Benefits and Beneficiary Nominations
steps.html:
• Public-service employees permanently incapable of continuing regular employment due to physical or mental illness can apply for Invalidity Benefits under section 33 of the Public Service Social Security Fund (PSSSF) Act 2018 (submitting Form PS-BEN.3, employer verification, and Medical Board certification; ordinary statutory eligibility requires at least 36 monthly contributions with 12 in the preceding year) [7].
  • Private-sector contributors enrolled in the National Social Security Fund (NSSF) should contact NSSF member services to verify contribution histories, review permanent incapacity benefit rules, and submit updated dependant and nominee registration records [8].

steps.title: Civil Identity, Tax Records, and Mainland vs Zanzibar Distinction
steps.html:
• Confirm that national identity particulars, birth records, and marriage certificates match across Mainland Tanzania registries via RITA (or its online eRITA portal) or in Zanzibar through the Zanzibar Civil Status Registration Agency (ZCSRA), which handles civil status record updates via district offices in Unguja and Pemba [3][5].
  • Assemble Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) documents with the Tanzania Revenue Authority (TRA), land titles or occupancy certificates, bank mandate records, and private insurance contracts in an indexed folder alongside will storage receipts [11].

steps.title: Cross-Border Document Authentication (Non-Apostille)
steps.html:
• Tanzania is not a Contracting Party to the HCCH 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, so Apostille certificates do not authenticate Tanzanian documents abroad [12].
  • Certified medical reports, notarized powers of attorney, and civil certificates required overseas must undergo authentication by the Legal Unit of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and East African Cooperation in Dodoma (or its designated department in Zanzibar), followed by diplomatic legalization at the destination country's embassy [6].

contacts.name: Ministry of Health
contacts.note: P.O. Box 743, Dodoma; curative hospital services, patient charters, and clinical oversight.

contacts.name: Registration, Insolvency and Trusteeship Agency (RITA)
contacts.note: RITA Tower, Dar es Salaam; Mainland civil records, will drafting guidance, and will custody.

contacts.name: Zanzibar Civil Status Registration Agency (ZCSRA)
contacts.note: Flamingo, Migombani, Zanzibar; Zanzibar civil status records and eCRVS updates.

contacts.name: Public Service Social Security Fund (PSSSF)
contacts.note: PSSSF House, Dodoma; public-sector invalidity benefits (Form PS-BEN.3) and beneficiary records.

contacts.name: National Social Security Fund (NSSF)
contacts.note: Benjamin Mkapa Pension Towers, Dar es Salaam; private-sector invalidity enquiries and dependant updates.

contacts.name: Tanzania Revenue Authority (TRA)
contacts.note: Dodoma / Dar es Salaam; Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) and tax administration.

contacts.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and East African Cooperation
contacts.note: Mtumba Area, P.O. Box 2933, Dodoma (and Zanzibar department); document authentication and consular legalization.
